newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold says Grootvlei hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: Randgold says Grootvlei hit by strike.

text.p: Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd said on Thursday that some 90 percent of the workers at its Grootvlei Proprietary Mines had gone on strike and that production had been affected.
Grootvlei general manager Neal Froneman said in a statement the employees, who began their strike on the night shift on Wednesday and continued early on Thursday, had made no demands to management.
The local National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) branch committee had told management they were unaware of the reasons for the action.

"Management and the NUM branch committee, together with regional NUM representatives, have been engaged in negotiations for the past six weeks regarding the future of the financially beleaguered mine, which has been hit by the gold price, unsatisfactory production levels and the substantial shortfall between its pumping costs and the state subsidy," Froneman said.
Grootvlei pumps and cleans water on behalf of all the gold mines east of Johannesburg.
Froneman said various ways of cutting costs and increasing revenue were being considered, but it was clear the mine's survival would require the retrenchment or redundancy of a number of employees.
Grootvlei, reported a net loss before capital spending of 29.16 million rand in the quarter to June 30 compared with a net loss of 1.5 million rand in the previous quarter.
